# Results — Study 644 (CPI-Day-Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **CPI-print
mornings (8:30 am ET, before the open) are a scheduled macro event that moves stocks and bonds
systematically**: the single input the Fed's post-2021 reaction function has watched most
closely should move SPY and TLT more than an average day, in a direction the market can bank.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprints `3ebc1d6324c3` (SPY) / `745c19792ff8` (TLT).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY raw OHLC + adjusted close (7,419 rows), 1997-01-02 → 2026-06-30; TLT raw OHLC + adjusted close (6,018 rows), 2002-07-30 → 2026-06-30 (TLT inception) |
| CPI calendar | **hardcoded** table of **353 actual CPI release dates** 1997-01-14 → 2026-06-10 (BLS archived news-release index, cross-checked against the official `histreleasedates.pdf`; **identical table** to sibling study [602-macro-announcement-premium](../../602-macro-announcement-premium/)'s `CPI_DATES`) |
| Events | **353/353** release dates map onto the SPY tape (2 forward-mapped off a market holiday); **286** map onto the shorter TLT tape |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group splits (non-overlapping single-day events); **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the CPI-day dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on hit rates; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebos (two-sided for return, one-sided "louder" for range) |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention (tradability leg only): SPY entered at the **prior session's close** — the calendar is public months ahead, zero look-ahead — and exited at the CPI-day close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirks (named) | no November-2025 CPI release — the Sept-2025 report was delayed to 2025-10-24 by the federal shutdown and the Oct-2025 report was never separately published; the next release (2025-12-18) covered both months. CPI lands at 8:30 am ET, **before** the 9:30 am open — the close-to-close bar fully contains the reaction |

No survivorship: SPY and TLT are index-tracking ETFs, not survivor panels. TLT's shorter sample
(2002→) is named everywhere its numbers appear.

## The headline — CPI-day return vs all other days

| quantity | SPY CPI days | SPY other days | TLT CPI days | TLT other days |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean return (bps) | **+3.73** | +3.80 | **+5.24** | +1.26 |
| gap (bps) | **−0.07** | | **+3.98** | |
| Welch *t* | **−0.01** | | **+0.67** | |
| Newey-West *t* (5 lags) | **−0.01** | | **+0.67** | |
| hit rate (up) | 198/353 = **56.1%** (Wilson [50.9%, 61.2%]) | | 156/286 = **54.5%** (Wilson [48.8%, 60.2%]) | |

Neither asset shows a certifiable directional reaction to a CPI print: SPY's CPI-day return is
statistically indistinguishable from an ordinary day (*t* ≈ 0), and TLT's positive-looking gap
(+3.98 bps) sits far under the **t ≥ 2** bar. **Random-calendar placebo (SPY return, two-sided,
20,000 draws):** observed +3.73 bps vs placebo mean +3.87 bps (sd 6.34) → **p = 0.62605** —
utterly unremarkable next to a random calendar of the same size.

## Realized high-low range on the same days — where the real reaction lives

| metric | CPI days | other days | Welch *t* | one-sided placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY (H−L)/prev close | 1.392% | 1.346% | +0.82 | 0.18350 |
| **TLT (H−L)/prev close** | **1.001%** | 0.884% | **+2.70** | **0.00025** |

**Bonds are the loud ones, not stocks.** TLT's realized range is genuinely and robustly elevated
on CPI mornings — Welch *t* = **+2.70**, confirmed by a one-sided random-calendar placebo
(**p = 0.00025** over 20,000 draws) — while SPY's range gap is statistically nothing
(*t* = +0.82, placebo *p* = 0.18). This is the one leg of the claim that clears the desk's
**t ≥ 2** bar on the real tape: CPI mornings make the long bond swing harder, mechanically
consistent with a print that directly re-prices rate expectations; equities don't show the same
certified loudness.

## Event window — SPY return (bps) by session offset around the release

| offset | −3 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean bps | +4.94 | +3.66 | +8.01 | **+3.73** | −2.63 | +16.35 | +3.51 |
| Welch *t* | +0.27 | +0.11 | +0.65 | **+0.10** | −0.74 | +2.04 | +0.07 |

- **Pre-release run-up:** cumulative [−3..−1] is **+16.62 bps/event** at one-sample
  *t* = **+1.67** — suggestive but not certified.
- **Day +2** clears *t* = 2.04, but this is one flagged offset out of seven tested with no
  multiple-comparison correction (≈0.3 false positives expected by chance alone), it has no
  stated mechanism, and neighboring offsets (+1, +3) show nothing — treated as noise, not signal.
- **Day 0 itself is flat** (+3.73 bps, *t* = 0.10): whatever direction the market picks on a
  given CPI morning, it isn't systematic across 353 releases.

## Regime contrast — pre vs post 2022-01-01 (the Fed's Dec-2021 hawkish pivot)

*Justified split: the Fed's 2021-12-15 FOMC (accelerated taper, dot plot signaling 2022 hikes)
made every subsequent CPI print a direct input to the rate-hike reaction function — chosen from
the FOMC calendar, not fit to the return data.*

| leg | pre-2022 | post-2022 | Welch *t* of the difference |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY CPI-day return | +2.74 bps (n=300, *t*=−0.13) | +9.35 bps (n=53, *t*=+0.24) | **+0.30** |
| SPY CPI-day range | 1.391% (*t*=+0.36) | 1.398% (*t*=+1.33) | **+0.05** |

Neither leg shows a certified regime break: the point estimates barely move and the era
*difference* itself is nowhere near *t* = 2. Whatever changed about CPI's market salience since
2022, it isn't visible as a mean shift in SPY's own return or range.

## Third axis — is CPI day the SINGLE BIGGEST trading day of its calendar month?

*Tested, not eyeballed: for every month with a mapped CPI session, is that session's
|return| (or range) the single largest of the month? A random day in an average
21-session month clears this bar ~4.8% of the time by chance alone — the honest baseline.*

| metric | pre-2022 | post-2022 | null (chance) | Welch *t* of the diff (post − pre) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY \|return\| | 4.3% (Wilson [2.5%, 7.3%], n=300) | 9.4% (Wilson [4.1%, 20.3%], n=53) | 4.8% | +1.21 |
| SPY range | 4.7% (Wilson [2.8%, 7.7%], n=300) | 3.8% (Wilson [1.0%, 12.8%], n=53) | 4.8% | −0.31 |
| TLT \|return\| | 4.7% (Wilson [2.7%, 8.3%], n=233) | 7.5% (Wilson [3.0%, 17.9%], n=53) | 4.8% | +0.72 |
| **TLT range** | 8.2% (Wilson [5.3%, 12.4%], n=233) | **15.1%** (Wilson [7.9%, 27.1%], n=53) | 4.8% | **+1.31** |

Every point estimate moves in the "more true since 2022" direction, and TLT range is the closest
to a real regime break — but **none of the four differences clears the *t* ≥ 2 bar**, and even
the best post-2022 rate (TLT range, 15.1% of months) is a small minority, nowhere close to
literally "the biggest day of the month." The folklore is directionally plausible and
statistically unconfirmed.

## Tradability — a naive "own SPY only on CPI day" timer

Enter the prior close (calendar public months ahead — zero look-ahead), exit the CPI-day close;
353 scheduled releases since 1997.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| gross per event | +3.73 bps |
| net per event (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **−6.27 / −16.27 bps** (≈ **−0.75% / −1.95%/yr** at 12 events) |
| all-other-days SPY mean | +3.80 bps |
| Welch *t* (CPI vs other days) | **−0.01** |
| hit rate | 56.1% |
| worst single CPI day | **−6.6%** |

There is no gross edge to begin with (+3.73 bps vs a +3.80 bp baseline — literally a coin flip
against the market's own average day), so costs turn a non-edge negative. The one certified
effect on this tape — TLT's elevated realized range — isn't monetizable with a directionless
long/short position; harvesting "loudness" without a view on direction needs an options/vol
instrument, which this study doesn't test, and which (by the precedent of the FOMC vol-crush
study, [637-fomc-vol-crush](../../637-fomc-vol-crush/)) tends to have the scheduled event
premium pre-priced by market makers ahead of the print in the first place.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased on BOTH axes

Deterministic daily-return process with scheduled pseudo-CPI days every 21st business day and
TWO independently tunable planted effects: a return-mean shift and a volatility multiplier; no
network.

| world | Welch *t* (return) | Welch *t* (range) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (mu_shift=0, vol_mult=1), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.24** (sd 1.26), \|t\|≥2 in 2/20 | mean **−0.11** (sd 0.91), \|t\|≥2 in 0/20 |
| planted return shift = +15 bps (seed 644) | **+3.46** | — |
| planted vol multiplier = 1.6× (seed 644) | +0.87 (should stay small) | **+13.07** |

The detector recovers a planted return shift without manufacturing a range signal, and recovers
a planted volatility multiplier without manufacturing a return signal — the two axes are
detected independently, exactly as the real-tape split (real on TLT range, none on return)
requires the machinery to be capable of. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Real on one leg, none on the rest: TLT's realized range is genuinely
  elevated on CPI mornings (Welch *t* = **+2.70**, one-sided placebo **p = 0.00025**) — bonds
  get louder, mechanically consistent with a print that directly re-prices rate expectations.
  Everything else is a statistical zero: SPY return (*t* = −0.01), TLT return (*t* = +0.67) and
  SPY's own range (*t* = +0.82, placebo *p* = 0.18) all fail the **t ≥ 2** bar, and the
  random-calendar placebo on SPY return (*p* = 0.63) confirms it's unremarkable.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No directional edge exists to harvest (SPY CPI-day timer nets
  **−6.27 bps/event** at 5 bps costs, ≈ **−0.75%/yr**); the one certified effect (TLT range)
  isn't monetizable without an options/vol view, which we don't test and which the FOMC
  precedent (637) suggests is pre-priced ahead of the print anyway.
- **"CPI day is the biggest day of the month"? — BUSTED.** Every metric moves in the "more true
  since 2022" direction, but none of the four pre/post differences clears *t* = 2 (best case:
  TLT range, *t* = +1.31), and even the best post-2022 rate (15.1% of months for TLT range) is a
  small minority — nowhere near literally "the" biggest day. Directionally plausible, not
  statistically confirmed.
